instance.description: The instance to create the backup schedule on.
instance.rationale: This is a required reference to the parent Spanner instance. It does not directly introduce a security risk but must be correctly configured to ensure the backup schedule targets the intended instance.

database.description: The database to create the backup schedule on.
database.rationale: This is a required reference to the target database. It does not directly introduce a security risk but must be correctly configured to ensure backups are created for the intended database.

name.description: A unique identifier for the backup schedule, which cannot be changed after the backup schedule is created.
name.rationale: The backup schedule name is an optional identifier. It does not directly introduce a security risk but should follow naming conventions for clarity.

spec.description: Defines specifications of the backup schedule.
spec.rationale: The spec defines the backup frequency. It does not directly introduce a security risk but should be configured to meet the organisation's recovery point objectives.

cron_spec.rationale: The cron spec defines backup frequency. It does not directly introduce a security risk but should be set to ensure backups occur regularly.

full_backup_spec.description: The schedule creates only full backups.
full_backup_spec.rationale: Full backup spec determines the backup type. It does not directly introduce a security risk.

incremental_backup_spec.description: The schedule creates incremental backup chains.
incremental_backup_spec.rationale: Incremental backup spec determines the backup type. It does not directly introduce a security risk.

encryption_config.description: Configuration for the encryption of the backup schedule.
encryption_config.rationale: Configuring encryption for backups ensures that backup data is protected at rest. Using customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) provides greater control over data access and meets compliance requirements.

encryption_type.description: The encryption type of backups created by the backup schedule. Possible values are: USE_DATABASE_ENCRYPTION, GOOGLE_DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION, CUSTOMER_MANAGED_ENCRYPTION.
encryption_type.rationale: Setting encryption_type to CUSTOMER_MANAGED_ENCRYPTION ensures backups are protected using customer-controlled keys, providing greater security and compliance control over backup data.

kms_key_name.description: The resource name of the Cloud KMS key to use for encryption.
kms_key_name.rationale: Specifying a KMS key name is required when using CUSTOMER_MANAGED_ENCRYPTION. Without it, backups cannot use customer-controlled keys, reducing control over data protection.

kms_key_names.description: Fully qualified name of the KMS keys to use to encrypt this database.
kms_key_names.rationale: Specifying KMS key names ensures backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys across multiple locations, meeting compliance and data protection requirements.

project.description: If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project field is optional and defaults to the provider project. It does not directly introduce a security risk but should be explicitly set to avoid deploying resources to unintended projects.

cron_spec.description: Defines the cron schedule for the backup.
cron_spec.rationale: The cron spec defines backup timing. It does not directly introduce a security risk but should be configured to meet recovery point objectives.

text.description: Textual representation of the crontab. Allowed frequencies are 12 hour, 1 day, 1 week and 1 month.
text.rationale: The cron text defines backup frequency. It does not directly introduce a security risk but should be set to ensure backups occur at appropriate intervals.
